_readme: Does extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma (EMC) carry inactivating TSC1 or TSC2 alterations often enough to make an mTOR inhibitor a reachable option for a subset? Probed 2026-08-24; nobody in this repository had asked before. THIS FILE IS THE ONE HOME for every number the probe produced. The prompt was a single JSMO 2025 case abstract (registry citation galitskiy2025emcpembrolizumab) reporting TSC2 gene loss in an EWSR1::NR4A3 EMC whose TSC2 finding was never acted on, because the patient responded to pembrolizumab.
_not_medical_advice: A record of database and registry reads. NOT medical advice. Nothing here claims that any agent works, is safe, is selective, has a therapeutic window, or is clinically ready in EMC or in any patient. An eligibility criterion that admits a histology on paper says nothing about whether a particular person should enrol; a trial team decides that after its own review.
headline: EMC does carry TSC2-inactivating alterations, and they are RARE rather than absent: 1 of 75 sequenced EMC samples (1.33%, 95% CI 0.03-7.21%) carries a somatic TSC2 nonsense mutation, and 0 of 75 carries a TSC1 mutation. This is a MEASUREMENT, not a literature inference, and it is the first TSC1/TSC2 frequency for this disease that this repository is aware of.

question.primary: How often does EMC carry a pathogenic inactivating TSC1 or TSC2 alteration?
question.secondary: If such a subset exists, could it reach an open trial or another access route?
question.why_mechanistic: TSC1/TSC2 form the brake on mTORC1; inactivating alterations release it. The link to an mTOR inhibitor is mechanistic rather than correlative, which is why a frequency was worth measuring.

measurement._what: cBioPortal public API, read on a GitHub Actions runner. EMC is a codable OncoTree type (EMCHS), so samples can be counted directly instead of inferred from prose.
measurement._sample_vs_patient: cBioPortal rows are SAMPLES. One patient can contribute more than one. The count below is therefore an upper bound on patients, and the two MSK cohorts almost certainly overlap each other and overlap the 18-patient series PMID 40828003. Do not add the cohorts together.

cohorts.study_name: Soft Tissue and Bone Sarcoma (MSK, Nat Commun 2022)
cohorts.assay: MSK-IMPACT targeted matched tumour-normal DNA panel
cohorts.copy_number_note: HTTP 404 'Molecular profile not found: sarcoma_msk_2022_cna'. This cohort cannot answer the gene-LOSS question at all, only the MUTATION question.

cohorts.study_name: MSK-IMPACT 50K Clinical Sequencing Cohort (MSK, Cancer Cell 2026)
cohorts.assay: MSK-IMPACT targeted matched tumour-normal DNA panel; GISTIC discrete copy number

cohorts.note: counted for completeness; TSC status not separately queried, and it overlaps the two above

the_one_positive.why_it_counts: A somatic nonsense mutation is a truncating, inactivating alteration - the class PRECISION 1 and the MD Anderson trial both require, not a variant of unknown significance.

verification_round_6._why: The whole measured frequency rests on this one sample, so it was checked against the record rather than trusted because the query returned cleanly.

two_independent_histology_fields_agree.cohort_wide_agreement: 75 samples by ONCOTREE_CODE=EMCHS, 75 by CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED, intersection 75, symmetric difference 0. The denominator does not rest on one string in one column.

patient_level._note: the diagnosis was revised to EMC, so the label is a considered call rather than a default

sample_level._consistency: 4 mutations and TMB 0.13 are consistent with EMC's reported quiet genome; 77% purity means the variant call is not a low-fraction artefact
sample_level._inconsistency_in_the_record: sampleType says Primary Solid Tumor while SAMPLE_TISSUE says Lymph Node. Noted, not resolved; it does not affect the histology call.

verification_round_6.⛔_the_real_caveat: MATCHED_STATUS = Unmatched. This sample was NOT sequenced against a matched normal, so although the mutation record carries mutationStatus 'Somatic', somatic status here is INFERRED BY FILTERING rather than demonstrated. A germline TSC2 Q955* would mean tuberous sclerosis, which is clinically conspicuous and makes that reading unlikely - but 'unlikely' is not 'excluded', and the one data point the frequency rests on is therefore somatic-by-inference.
verification_round_6.structural_variant_check_not_obtained: EMC is defined by NR4A3 rearrangement and this cohort has a structural-variant profile, so an NR4A3 fusion in this sample would have confirmed the histology a third way. All three candidate GET shapes for that endpoint returned HTTP 404, so it was not obtained. Recorded as NOT DONE rather than as a negative.

tsc1_or_tsc2_homozygous_deletion.note: the 15 are the EMC samples in the only queried cohort that HAS a copy-number profile

rates._ci_method: Clopper-Pearson exact binomial, alpha=0.05, computed from the counts in this file

the_control_that_makes_a_zero_meaningful._why: A count of zero is a reading of ABSENCE only if the genes were on the panel that was run; otherwise zero means NOT LOOKED FOR, which is a different statement (CLAUDE.md section 4).
the_control_that_makes_a_zero_meaningful.verdict: PASSES. TSC1 and TSC2 are on every MSK-IMPACT panel version including the smallest (341 genes), and every sample in msk_impact_50k_2026 carries both mutation and CNA data (all_cases_with_mutation_and_cna_data = 54331). The zeros are readings of absence.

what_this_measurement_still_cannot_see: SINGLE-COPY (shallow) loss. The discrete copy-number profile stores only homozygous deletion (-2) and amplification (2); there is no -1 state in the payload. The index case's reported 'TSC2 gene loss' may well BE a single-copy loss, in which case this measurement would not have counted it. That is the single largest gap between what was measured and what the index case reported.
Promoter, deep-intronic, structural and epigenetic inactivation, none of which a targeted exonic panel calls.
Protein-level inactivation with an intact gene.

additional_cohorts_round_5._why: The 75 came from one institution on one assay. These add count, and two of them add independence.
additional_cohorts_round_5.⛔_never_add_these_together: sarcoma_msk_2022 uses anonymised study-prefixed sample ids (e.g. sarcoma_msk_2022-2691) while msk_impact_50k_2026 uses real MSK P-ids (e.g. P-0000379-T02-IM3). The MSK cohorts therefore CANNOT be deduplicated against each other and their EMC counts must not be summed. Only the non-MSK cohorts are independent of the 75.
additional_cohorts_round_5.control: PASSES for every cohort above: each has all samples in its mutation sample list, and each shows hundreds (or, for the small sarcoma cohort, tens) of TSC1- and TSC2-mutated samples study-wide, which proves both genes are on the assay. The EMC zeros are readings of absence.
additional_cohorts_round_5.⭐_independent_replication: 0 of 11 EMC samples in two non-MSK cohorts (pan_origimed_2020 and pancan_pdmr_2025) carry a TSC1 or TSC2 mutation. Small, but it is independent of the 75 and it is consistent with a low single-digit rate rather than with a PEComa-like 36%.

the_single_copy_question._status: STILL OPEN after round 5; round 7 dispatched against the right instrument.
the_single_copy_question.round_5_result: HETLOSS was requested for TSC1 and TSC2 from msk_impact_50k_2026's GISTIC profile and returned ZERO records STUDY-WIDE - across all 54,331 samples and every gene, not just EMC.
the_single_copy_question.⛔_what_that_actually_means: NOT 'no EMC has single-copy TSC loss'. It means THAT PROFILE STORES NO -1 STATE AT ALL. Reading the EMC count alone (0 of 15) would have yielded exactly the wrong conclusion, stated confidently. The study-wide count is what caught it, and that check is the reason it is recorded here as an open question rather than as a second zero.
the_single_copy_question.the_right_instrument: pancan_pdmr_2025 carries a log2CNA profile - continuous copy number rather than a thresholded call - and holds 9 EMC samples. Requested in round 7.
the_single_copy_question.why_it_matters: The index case reported TSC2 gene LOSS. If that is a single-copy loss, nothing measured so far would have counted it.

literature_bound._what: What the published record contains, established so that 'nobody has reported this' is a count rather than a recollection.

the_hitcounts_are_full_text_co_mention_n._method: Europe PMC indexes open-access FULL TEXT, so a hit can be a paper that names EMC in one table and TSC1 in another. The discriminating test is whether both appear in the ABSTRACT.

positive_control_emc_and_pecoma._why_this_matters: The same test returns 3 for EMC-and-PEComa, which is expected because the two appear together in differential-diagnosis abstracts. So the test is not simply returning zero for everything; the zeros above are real.

the_purpose_built_study.title: Secondary Genetic Alterations in Extraskeletal Myxoid Chondrosarcoma
the_purpose_built_study.design: 18 EMC patients (20 samples) on MSK-IMPACT 341-505 gene panel, matched tumour-normal, fusion subtype confirmed by Archer FusionPlex and/or FISH
the_purpose_built_study.its_own_claim: 'This is the first study addressing the genomic landscape in EMC with regard to prognostication beyond fusion subtypes and histology.'
the_purpose_built_study.what_it_reports: All cases low TMB (0-2, mean 0.83). Two-thirds had concurrent secondary genetic alterations (0-8, mean 1.67 per case). Only TP53 alterations were recurrent (2 cases). Other non-recurrent alterations involved CDKN1B, TERT and MET 'among others'.
the_purpose_built_study._the_honest_limit: 'among others' is not an enumeration, so a single non-recurrent TSC alteration could sit inside it unnamed. This is precisely why the cBioPortal measurement above was worth taking: it counts rather than reads.
the_purpose_built_study._overlap_warning: MSK-IMPACT, MSK institution - these 18 patients are very likely inside the 75 samples counted above. Treat as the same evidence seen twice, not as independent confirmation.

emc_sequencing_papers_already_held_here.note: reports no TSC1/TSC2 anywhere in the full text; only PTEN appears, in a passage listing tumour suppressors on chromosome 10q

'Somatic point mutations were identified (total calls ranging from 2-26) but were of unknown significance'; 'Exome copy number analysis did not detect clinically significant focal amplifications or deletions'

_list: PMC9890057 (AACR GENIE, histology-agnostic targets in sarcoma)
pan_sarcoma_cgp_full_texts_checked._conclusion: Not one of eleven pan-sarcoma comprehensive-genomic-profiling papers links EMC to TSC1/TSC2 or to mTOR. The richest of them names EMC 17 times and reports only the fusion for it.

aacr_genie_ultrarare_sarcoma_paper._why_the_full_text_404s: not open access; its Europe PMC fullTextXML returns HTTP 404. The abstract was read from the Europe PMC record instead.
aacr_genie_ultrarare_sarcoma_paper.n: 1407 ultra-rare sarcomas from AACR GENIE, via cBioPortal
aacr_genie_ultrarare_sarcoma_paper.what_it_names: most commonly mutated gene TP53; commonest CNVs CDKN2A/CDKN2B deletion and MDM2/CDK4 amplification; TMB generally low

reachability._verdict: YES, and this is a correction to the premise the probe started from. PRECISION 1 is closed to accrual, but it is not the only route and its closure does not make the question moot: at least two trials that explicitly match TSC1/TSC2 to an mTOR inhibitor are RECRUITING, an expanded-access programme names the same genotype, and nab-sirolimus is an approved drug.

routes.name: PRECISION 1
routes.detail: Phase 2 tumour-agnostic basket, nab-sirolimus, 'malignant solid tumors harbouring pathogenic inactivating alterations in TSC1 or TSC2 genes', age >=12, enrollment 120 estimated, primary completion estimated 2024-12-31, completion estimated 2025-12-31.
routes._note: EMC would have been eligible on histology; the trial is simply no longer accruing. Its last posted update is 2024-06-03, which is stale relative to this read.

routes.name: TAPUR
routes.detail: 'Group 6 (mTOR, TSC)': participants receive temsirolimus per label; acceptable genomic matches include mTOR, TSC1/2, AKT1 mutations. Conditions include advanced solid tumours.
routes._why_this_is_the_strongest_route: recruiting, recently updated, 181 US sites, and the arm names TSC1/2 explicitly.

routes.name: Gemcitabine + nab-sirolimus in LMS or STS with TSC1/TSC2 loss-of-function
routes.detail: Inclusion 1: 'histologically confirmed leiomyosarcoma or sarcoma with TSC2 or TSC1 loss-of-function mutations or deletions based on standard-of-care genomic testing.' EMC is a soft-tissue sarcoma, so the criterion admits it.
routes._note: Phase 1, single site, 18 patients estimated - narrow, but open and directly on point. The same institution treated the index case.

routes.name: Expanded access for ABI-009
routes.open_to_an_emc_patient: UNKNOWN - the record is 4 years stale
routes.detail: Admits 'any other malignancy with activation in any mTOR pathway component ... or an identified relevant rare genetic mutation in mTOR pathway genes, including but not limited to TSC1, TSC2, PIK3CA, PTEN, for which there are no FDA-approved treatments or no other comparable or satisfactory alternative therapies available.' EMC has no FDA-approved treatment.
routes._caveat: Last posted update 2022-03-16. Whether the programme is still operating is NOT established by this read and must not be asserted from it.

routes.name: CAPTUR
routes.detail: 'Group 10 Arm CLOSED' - the temsirolimus arm, whose gene list includes TSC1 and TSC2, is explicitly closed. The trial recruits; this arm does not.

routes.name: MOST / molecular-triage maintenance
routes.detail: The everolimus arm, which names 'TSC1, TSC2 or PTEN loss', is labelled 'Closed cohort'.

the_approved_drug.generic: sirolimus protein-bound particles for injectable suspension (nab-sirolimus)
the_approved_drug.indication: 'the treatment of adult patients with locally advanced unresectable or metastatic malignant perivascular epithelioid cell tumor (PEComa)'
the_approved_drug._what_this_means: There is no tumour-agnostic TSC1/TSC2 indication. The drug exists and is approved, so an off-label route is conceivable, but the label does not support EMC and this file makes no claim that it should be used there.
the_approved_drug.dosing_on_label: 100 mg/m2 IV over 30 minutes on days 1 and 8 of each 21-day cycle

how_good_is_the_biomarker._why_this_section: The route's value depends not only on how many EMC patients carry the alteration but on how strong the alteration-to-response link actually is. All figures below are VERBATIM from the primary full texts, not from a search summary.

ampect_primary.n: 34 treated (safety), 31 efficacy-evaluable, 25 with tumour mutation profiling
ampect_primary.tsc2_altered: 36% (9 of 25) had TSC2 mutations or deletions
ampect_primary.headline_biomarker_comparison: 'Eighty-nine percent (8 of 9) of patients with a TSC2 mutation achieved a confirmed response versus 13% (2 of 16) without a TSC2 mutation (P < .001, Fisher's exact).'
ampect_primary.the_tsc1_arm: 'Additional confirmed PRs were seen in 20% (1 of 5) of patients with a TSC1 mutation, and in 9% (1 of 11) without a mutation in TSC1 or TSC2.'
ampect_primary.independent_predictor_that_is_not_a_geno: 'Responses occurred in 59% (10 of 17) of patients with pS6+ tumors versus 0 of eight patients with pS6- tumors; the absence of pS6 staining was a negative predictor of response (P = .008, Fisher's exact).' On multivariate analysis only TSC2-inactivating mutations (P < .001) and pS6 expression (P = .004) were associated with response.
ampect_primary.the_paper_s_own_caveat: 'it remains unclear as to why TSC2 mutations and not TSC1 mutations were associated with response in this study. This analysis is limited by the small number of patients (n = 5) with TSC1-mutant tumors.'
ampect_primary.erratum: PMID 37890128, PMC10713098, doi 10.1200/jco.23.02173, J Clin Oncol 2023;41(35). The primary full text carries it only as a 'correction-forward' link; the biomarker passages quoted above stand in the primary text as retrieved.

ampect_long_term.orr_final: 38.7% (95% CI 21.8 to 57.8) by independent radiologist review, RECIST v1.1

the_counterweight.title: The Impact of TSC-1 and -2 Mutations on Response to Therapy in Malignant PEComa: A Multicenter Retrospective Analysis
the_counterweight.finding: 'No significant differences in survival were identified between TSC-1 and TSC-2 mutated PEComa or TSC-1/-2 versus other mutations. No significant difference was seen in progression-free survival after first-line therapy between mTOR inhibition versus other systemic therapies.'
the_counterweight.its_own_size: 2 patients with TSC-1 mutations and 12 with TSC-2 mutations; only one of the TSC-1-mutated tumours received mTOR inhibition
the_counterweight.how_to_read_it: UNDERPOWERED, so this is weak evidence rather than counter-evidence. It should not be quoted as refuting AMPECT's biomarker; it should be quoted as showing the biomarker has not been independently reproduced in a well-powered retrospective.

how_good_is_the_biomarker.transferability_to_emc: NOT ESTABLISHED, and nothing in this file establishes it. Every biomarker figure above is from PEComa. AMPECT's nine TSC2-mutant responders had primary sites in retroperitoneum (3), kidney (2), uterus (2), liver (1) and small bowel (1) - all PEComa sites, none an EMC site. Whether a TSC2-inactivating EMC behaves like a TSC2-inactivating PEComa is an open question that this probe did not and could not answer.

mtorc1_output_axis_in_emc._what: A speculative thread carried into the probe: mTORC1 drives HIF1A and VEGF, and EMC's most reproducible clinical signal is sensitivity to antiangiogenic TKIs, so perhaps the mTORC1 output axis reads live in EMC. Graded here rather than left hanging.
mtorc1_output_axis_in_emc._source_of_every_number: research/modalities/emc-expression-panels.json -> gene_reads. That file OWNS the per-platform means and percentiles; only the cross-platform DERIVED comparison lives here.
platforms: GSE24369 / GPL6244: 6 EMC vs 29 comparator sarcomas
verdict: The DIRECTION replicates for RPS6, HIF1A and VEGFA across two platforms, and does NOT replicate for MTOR or AKT1, which flip sign. So the downstream output genes read modestly higher in EMC than in comparator sarcomas while the pathway-core genes give no consistent signal.

THE PERCENTILE FRAMING WAS MISLEADING AND IS WITHDRAWN HERE. HIF1A sits at the 98th percentile of GPL6244's own probe distribution in EMC - but the COMPARATOR arm sits at the 97th on the same array, and on GPL3290 the EMC value is at the 42nd. The striking percentile is a property of the platform, not of EMC; the EMC-versus-comparator gap is 0.23 standard deviations.
The effect sizes are small (0.15 to 0.93 z-units) on 6 and 10 EMC samples.
mtorc1_output_axis_in_emc.what_it_cannot_do_for_this_route: NOTHING, in either direction. Abundance is not activation; a transcript is not a phosphoprotein; and no transcript reading can establish a pathogenic inactivating DNA alteration, which is what the trials require and what the biomarker means. AMPECT's own output-axis predictor was pS6 by IMMUNOHISTOCHEMISTRY, which is a phospho-protein stain and is not what RPS6 transcript abundance measures. The thread is recorded as bounded, and it is not carried forward as support for the route.
mtorc1_output_axis_in_emc.adding_tsc_genes_to_the_expression_panel: NOT WORTH DOING FOR THIS QUESTION. TSC1 and TSC2 are absent from research/modalities/emc-expression-panels.json gene_reads, and adding them is cheap (CPU only). But expression is not inactivation: a low TSC2 transcript could not establish the alteration, and the DNA question has now been answered directly and better by the cBioPortal measurement above.

index_case.registry_citation: galitskiy2025emcpembrolizumab, added to research/data/emc-clinical-registry.json in this same branch - it was NOT previously recorded there despite being described as such
index_case._europe_pmc_note: hitCount 0 for a title search; conference-supplement abstracts are not indexed there
index_case.authors_affiliated_to_the_assay_vendor: 13 of 16, counted from the author list and affiliation superscripts on the sponsor's publication page
index_case.what_it_reported: microsatellite stable, TMB 0.67 mut/Mb, TSC2 gene loss; immune-enriched/fibrotic tumour microenvironment with high PD-L1 by RNA-seq
index_case.what_was_done: pembrolizumab after molecular tumour board review; 15 cycles; near-complete response reported, no progression at the time of writing
index_case.what_was_not_done: the TSC2 finding was never acted on therapeutically, and the report gives it no functional or protein-level confirmation and no denominator (how many EMC were profiled is not stated)
index_case._alteration_class_mismatch: The case reports gene LOSS. The measurement above found a MUTATION in 1 of 75 and homozygous DELETION in 0 of 15. If the case's 'loss' is a single-copy deletion, the measurement would not have counted it - see measurement.what_this_measurement_still_cannot_see.

retrieval.why_ci: the dev sandbox egress proxy answers 403 to CONNECT for www.ebi.ac.uk, clinicaltrials.gov and eutils (CLAUDE.md section 6)
failures_and_what_each_MEANS: ft_genie_ultrarare_sarcoma_full 404 - PMC11874058 is not open access. A fact about the paper, not a fetch problem.
genie_cbio_studies / genie_cbio_cancer_types 401 - genie.cbioportal.org requires authentication. The public cbioportal.org instance was used instead and answered everything needed.
cbio_*_mut_all 400 'Request parameter is missing: entrezGeneId' - the endpoint requires a gene; corrected in round 4.
cbio_sarcoma_msk_2022_cna_all 404 'Molecular profile not found' - that cohort HAS no copy-number profile. This is a finding, and it is recorded in the measurement section rather than discarded.
ft_ampect_erratum_2023 404 - PMC10713098 is not open access.

The discrete-copy-number endpoint IGNORED its entrezGeneId parameter and returned the whole profile (156,526 records, byte-identical for both gene requests). Filtering was therefore done locally on entrezGeneId. A caller that trusted the parameter would have counted every gene's deletions as TSC's.

corrections_to_the_premises_this_probe_s._why_this_section: The probe was handed a set of figures explicitly flagged as unverified WebSearch summaries, with an instruction to treat every one as UNVERIFIED until checked against a primary record. Four did not survive the check. Recorded so the next reader inherits the corrected version and can see what a search summary does to a number.

items.premise: The case is already recorded in research/data/emc-clinical-registry.json under citation id galitskiy2025emcpembrolizumab.
items.what_is_true: No such citation existed, and no handle for the case - author, DOI, sponsor, conference - appeared anywhere in the repository. The retrieval had been done and cached on the literature-cache branch and never promoted. It is now in the registry.
items.how_checked: grep for galitskiy, bostongene, the DOI and JSMO across the whole tree, plus the registry's own citations map (23 ids, none of them this one)

items.premise: 15 of 17 authors employed by the company whose assay is the subject.
items.what_is_true: 13 of 16. Counted from the author list and affiliation superscripts on the sponsor's own publication page: 13 carry superscript 1 (BostonGene Corporation), 3 carry superscript 2 (MD Anderson Cancer Center), none is unmarked.
items._note: The direction of the conflict-of-interest point is unchanged; only the figure was wrong.

items.premise: PRECISION 1 (NCT05103358): open, registration-intent, tumour-agnostic phase 2 basket.
items.what_is_true: ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING, last posted update 2024-06-03, estimated completion 2025-12-31. Everything else about it in the premise checks out against the record: tumour-agnostic, pathogenic inactivating TSC1/TSC2, age >=12, 120 estimated enrolment, 100 mg/m2 IV days 1 and 8 of a 21-day cycle, primary endpoint ORR by independent radiographic review.
items._and_the_consequence_did_not_follow: The premise also said a closed trial makes the reachability argument moot. It does not - see reachability. Two other trials that match TSC1/TSC2 to an mTOR inhibitor are recruiting.

items.premise: AMPECT exploratory biomarker analysis: 8/9 (89%) patients with inactivating TSC2 alterations responded, versus 1/5 (20%) for TSC1.
items.status: TWO REAL NUMBERS, PAIRED INTO A COMPARISON THE PAPER DOES NOT MAKE
items.what_is_true: Both figures appear in the primary text, but they are not each other's comparator. The paper's stated comparison is 89% (8 of 9) with a TSC2 mutation versus 13% (2 of 16) WITHOUT a TSC2 mutation (P < .001, Fisher's exact). The 1-of-5 figure is a separate sentence: 'Additional confirmed PRs were seen in 20% (1 of 5) of patients with a TSC1 mutation, and in 9% (1 of 11) without a mutation in TSC1 or TSC2.'
items.why_it_matters: The paired version reads as a head-to-head showing TSC2 beats TSC1, on n=5. The paper explicitly declines that reading: 'it remains unclear as to why TSC2 mutations and not TSC1 mutations were associated with response in this study. This analysis is limited by the small number of patients (n = 5) with TSC1-mutant tumors.'

items.premise: AMPECT: ORR 38.7%, median PFS 10.6 months, median duration of response 39.7 months.
items.status: CONFIRMED against the primary record, with one clarification
items.what_is_true: Those three are the 2024 long-term update's figures (PMID 38427923). The 2021 primary report (PMID 34637337) gives ORR 39% (12 of 31) and median OS 40.8 months, with median DOR not reached. Quoting 38.7% and 39.7 months together is correct only against the 2024 paper.
